verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents delivering raw events to ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake and S3, with tables auto-created. Profile Builder writes customer profiles into your warehouse, and a community user confirms collecting data into BigQuery. The 'schedule I control' part is not shown: delivery is real-time streaming or micro-batching chosen by what the destination prefers, and 'optional batching' is mentioned without any user-configurable cadence. The cron-based connector syncs pull third-party sources in, which is not scheduled event or profile delivery. missing for 10: documented user-controlled delivery schedule or batch frequency for event/profile loads, independent corroboration of Snowflake/ClickHouse/S3 delivery and of profiles landing in the warehouse.

support.subject: As a data engineer, raw events and profiles land in my own warehouse or lake (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, S3) on a schedule I control

citations.quote: Delivery to destinations — ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Postgres, S3, GCS, and dozens of SaaS tools, streamed or micro-batched depending on what the destination prefers.
Sub-second speed of data delivery to your warehouse. Optional batching is also supported
Profiles are customer records stored in your warehouse, based on the events data you send to Jitsu.
Jitsu will automatically create tables and columns in your warehouse based on the data you send
It was very easy and straightforward to get started, deploy and start collecting things (into BigQuery).
